subject: Pilot licensing tradeoff: temporary license vs hour-pool + staircase pricing
messages:
From: Eli Thompson <eli@atlas-robotics.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@atlas-robotics.com
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Request: short pilot extension and pricing options

Neha —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick follow-up from our side: the engineering team needs an extra two weeks to run an integration test that will spike token usage; we expect the extra run to consume ~30% more tokens than the original scope.

Two asks: could Redwood provide (A) a short, temporary license that gives us reserved capacity for the extra two weeks (so we avoid rate throttling), or (B) an hour-pool we can draw against with a stepped discount as usage increases? Procurement is also asking for a simple SOW amendment they can sign quickly.

I attached the POC usage report so you can see the projected delta. We need a commercial answer by EOD Thursday so we can sign and proceed.

Appreciate it —
Eli
Director of ML Engineering
Atlas Robotics

Attachments: POC_Usage_Report_Q3.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Eli Thompson <eli@atlas-robotics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 10:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: short pilot extension and pricing options

Eli —

Thanks for the clear ask and the usage detail. Two pragmatic options we can put in front of you quickly:

1) Temporary reserve (2-week license): reserved throughput on a medium instance group, guaranteed burst capacity up to the projected usage. Price: flat fee of $9,500 for the 14-day window. Includes priority routing and one on-call escalation during the window.

2) Hour-pool with staircase discounts: we provision an hour-pool (prepaid) you draw from. Base rate $60/hr; discounts kick in at thresholds (after 200 hours: 10% off, after 400 hours: 18% off). Estimated cost for your projected delta: ~$7,800 — if usage remains above the higher threshold we can rebate at reconciliation.

We can also do a hybrid: a smaller reserve + hour-pool for burst. I attached a short SOW amendment template and a CSV showing the price math.

If procurement wants a signed doc, contracts@atlas can review Draft_SOW-v2.pdf — we can accept the SOW amendment + a one-line PO to fast-track.

I'll loop in Marissa for any promotional flexibility; David can confirm the operational steps for a temporary reserve.

Next steps: Which option looks best to you? We can turn the SOW around same-day if you confirm.

—Neha
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

Attachments: Draft_SOW-v2.pdf (PDF), redwood-pricing-options-20261117.csv (CSV)
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: short pilot extension and pricing options

Neha / David —

Agree with the two options. A couple of negotiation notes for procurement:
- If Atlas signs for the temporary reserve we should hold list price but offer a $1,000 one‑time onboarding credit (gives them an immediate net saving and keeps LTV neat).
- For hour-pool: consider adding a 30% rebate cap rather than open-ended rebates to limit downside (we can reconcile after the pilot).
- Hybrid: offer a 10% discount on the hour-pool if they also take the reserve.

David — confirm we can spin the reserve within 8 hours from signed SOW and that the on-call escalation is covered.

If procurement pushes on a line-item discount we can flex up to 12% on the hybrid package for a signed PO before Thursday EOD.

—Marissa
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 11:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: short pilot extension and pricing options

Quick ops confirmation: we can provision a medium reserve within 8 hours but need a signed SOW + PO to scope the instance group. On-call escalation is the standard post-sales support rota (one responder during the 14-day window).

Technical note for Eli: the reserve gives you reserved slots but does not change token billing — you'll still be billed for token consumption at normal per-token rates; the reserve covers capacity (latency/throughput). The hour-pool is token-agnostic and billed as consumption of dedicated hours. Hybrid keeps token billing normal plus hour draw for burst orchestration.

I'll prepare the minimal ops checklist and attach below. If you confirm today we can schedule provisioning for Friday morning.

—David
VP, Infrastructure Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Ops_Reserve_Checklist.txt (text)
From: Eli Thompson <eli@atlas-robotics.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@atlas-robotics.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: short pilot extension and pricing options

Neha / Marissa / David —

Thanks — we reviewed internally. Procurement prefers the hybrid path (small reserve + hour-pool) so we avoid throttling risk but also cap short-term cost exposure. Eli from procurement will sign the amended SOW as soon as we get the 10% combined-discount on the hour-pool you mentioned.

Can you confirm final numbers (reserve fee + hour-pool estimate after 10% hybrid discount) in a one-line quote? We can attach a PO and route to contracts for a same-day signature.

Agree timeline: turn SOW, provision Friday morning, run the two-week spike next week.

Best,
Eli

On Fri, Nov 20, 2026 at 10:14 AM Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com> wrote:
> Eli —
>
> Confirming: hybrid path with a $8,550 blended hour-pool estimate (after 10% hybrid discount) + $8,500 reserve fee (reduced onboarding credit applied). One-line quote: Total $17,000 for the 14-day window + token billing per-line item.
>
> Draft SOW will be updated and uploaded to the Drive link. If that looks good I can have contracts@redwood create the PO-ready SOW and send to your contracts alias.
>
> —Neha
